questions.question: I’m not sure my dog is even trainable. Can you help?
questions.answer: Yes. There’s no judgement on your dog’s ability. Every dog is an individual, so we start where you are today and build from there, at a pace that suits you both.

questions.question: How does 1-1 training work?
questions.answer: It starts with an initial assessment to understand what you and your dog need, followed by a personalised training plan and private 1-hour sessions. You control the pace to fit around your schedule, and you can get phone support between sessions if you need advice.

questions.question: I’m getting a new puppy or rescue dog. When should I get in touch?
questions.answer: Before they arrive, if you can. A pre-puppy home visit covers puppy-proofing your home, the equipment and toys you’ll need, enrichment, and how to help your new dog settle in. After that I can help with toilet training, socialisation and more.

questions.question: Does my dog need any experience to start scentwork?
questions.answer: No experience is needed for the Bronze course, and it’s suitable for dogs of any age. Dogs from 7 months to 13 years old have taken part so far.

questions.question: Can we join Silver without doing Bronze?
questions.answer: Silver is for dogs who have completed a Bronze course, or have already done some scentwork training and feel ready to progress. Please have a chat with me before booking. Gold is open to Silver-level dogs only.

questions.question: Where are the scent detection courses held?
questions.answer: Outdoors at C & W Commercials, Western Way, Wednesbury, WS10 7BW. The extra space makes it ideal for dogs who need a little more room.

questions.question: What should I bring to a scent course?
questions.answer:
Your dog, a bowl, treats or a toy, a lead, harness or collar, and a sense of fun!

For Gold, also bring your scent tins from the Bronze course, plus an old pair of boots and an old jacket or jumper to use in the search areas.
